strings.TRI_undersea_riches_desc:
The Führer fought recklessly for Baku's oil, and the Duce turned greedy over Libya's black gold — out of necessity, the leadership of Trinidad also vested the nation's future on the petrochemical industry, and it had paid off dramatically. Though the exploitation of Trinidad's sizable oil reserve subsidizes the exorbitant cost of basic welfare and state investment, the bread and circus is also a hanging thread away from slipping into a cause for unrest, as most Trinis have grown reliant on the benefits.

Despite honeyed words from the north, the Anglos have stood as an opponent to Trinidad's independent state development due to the consequent decline of economic leverage. With Canada and the U.S. both actively attempting to wrestle away the state's control over its oil extraction, the survival of one of the Caribbean's better-off economies is uncertain.
strings.TRI_disunited_front_desc:
Eric Williams is out, to the shock of millions around the Caribbean, his once-illustrious legacy tossed into the mud by the will of a people furious with his inaction. In his place rises a large coalition of anti-Williams leftists and conservatives alike, united by their burning will to see Williams out and change come to Trinidad.

The problem, of course, is deciding what this change actually will be.

The unions, whose strike ground the economy to a halt, demand further protections and benefits for them and their workers. The leaders of the Army, whose mutiny struck the final blow and toppled the Williams regime, demand that power be put into apolitical hands - their hands - as loudly as their soldiers cry for change. The Black Power movement, whose protests started this chain of events, demand that their cries for social change are accepted and implemented.

In the middle of this whirlpool, it falls to the interim Daaga government to chart an impossible course through the chaos. The future path of Trinidad hinges on their success or failure.
strings.TRI_pnm_dominance_desc:
Trinidad is a democracy, undeniably, but it's hard to tell if one looks at the recent electoral results. The PNM dominates the political scene in every facet and position, disarming its opposition with an almost surgical precision. Led by the immensely popular Eric Williams, President and so-called “Father of the Nation”, the PNM has enjoyed consistent popularity since the formation of the WIF, and has no challengers to truly oppose it.

Of course, nothing lasts forever, and the nationalist, left-wing slant of the PNM has its fair share of opponents, as does Eric Williams himself. However, until these opponents are able to organize themselves - or until they're able to coax a majority of the people to their side - Eric Williams and the PNM look set to dominate the near future of Trinidad.
strings.TRI_Fragmented_Politics_desc:
In a politics defined by ethno-religious loyalties through discipline and stubbornness, Eric Williams' People's National Movement has barely edged out its rivals. The PNM, anchored in the Afro-Trinidadian working class and supported by elements of the island's unions and intelligentsia, finds itself pitted against a highly divided opposition, particularly among the substantial Indo-Trinidadian minority.

While William's claims to want to build a Trinidad for all its people, minorities already fear that the PNM behemoth will attempt to assert Afro-Trinidadian rule.While the opposition squabbles among itself, Williams has already been leveraging reforms ranging from social aspects to economic reform, focusing on reversing the long-lasting impacts of slavery on the islands.

Using these reforms as well as connections to unions and movement leaders, Williams continues to cement his power.
strings.TRI_OFN_Outpost_desc:
Rented to the United States by the Brits during the most desperate parts of the Second World War, Chaguaramas was a simple port constructed solely to maintain a presence over America's backyard, and of course, to alleviate the mounting debts the Royal Navy had incurred.

Throughout the years, however, as Europe proper became overrun by fascism and the OFN's focus shifted back towards its home turf, Chaguaramas had transformed into one of the most important anti-submarine fortifications across the Caribbean — particularly evident when U-boats devastated all semblances of a supply chain during the latter parts of the war.

Fitted nowadays with the best American naval expertise has to offer, it is less a beautiful jewelry to Trinidadians than a sore spot for its borderline colonial construction. But knowing that Washington won't see any trouble so long as the local bosses get paid well enough, it does seem rather pointless to abolish something amounting to little more than a relic.
strings.TRI_Beyond_Slavery_and_Capitalism_desc:
Following the course of many a revolutionary country, the East Caribbean Union has become a developmentalist economy, like that of Mexico's. Nationalizations, especially of Trinidadian oil, have become staple of the new state, with Trinidad being the first target of the new economic plan.

The funds gained from these nationalized industries are then spent on social programs or on the enrichment of the other, less developed, islands in the union. While many support the development of other islands, viewing it as positive to the economy of the union as a whole, some Trinidadians are angered by this policy, as they view their money not being spent on them.
strings.TRI_First_Among_Unequals_desc:
Worker's liberation isn't an easy path, at least not for the East Caribbeans. Like many of their fellow socialist nations, the Union has taken on a centralized approach to government, with the power coming from the oil-rich Trinidad. It seems that the other islands aren't as fond of the arrangement as Trinidad itself.

In Grenada, Tobago, St. Vincent, and the Grenadines, grumbles of the workers and their representatives can be heard across the ocean. Unfortunately for them, the Trinidad's oil goes far, and the other islands will just have to deal with Trinidad on top, at least for now.
strings.TRI_Doc_Knows_Best_desc:
Dr. Eric Williams, affectionately called “the Doc” by some of his followers, rules over {tri_getnamedef} with an approach somewhere between an iron fist and a velvet glove. Governing through an elaborate political machine and the force of his renowned charisma, Williams' ambitions are directed at something greater than he already has: the attainment of unity across the entire Caribbean.

A strident nationalist utterly convinced of the veracity of his beliefs, Williams has little patience for opposition. Democracy functions more or less as normal, but the Doc's influence is overwhelming, and his word—backed by loyal, devout supermajorities at all levels of government—is law. For better or for worse, the cult of personality around Eric Williams is the sun around which the universe of {tri_getname} politics revolves.
strings.TRI_Doc_Without_Borders_desc:
Dr. Eric Williams is affectionately called “the Doc” by some of his followers, a constituency that is larger than ever before in the aftermath of his successful repulse of what he has termed the “imperialist attempt to tear the East Caribbean Union apart in Grenada”. His name is venerated almost on a level with that of a George Washington or an Emperor Pedro, and his word is even more law in the East Caribbean Union than it already was.

Williams' latest project is a broader front among the nations and peoples of the Caribbean. Since the East Caribbean Union has been such a success, “the Doc” hopes to expand it and promote a general spirit of anti-imperialism on Mexican lines throughout the region. At the same time, Williams has built on his already omnipresent cult of personality, becoming more and more authoritarian in defense of his expansive vision.
strings.TRI_Generalissimo_Williams_desc:
After Eric Gairy's successful invasion of Grenada that split the island from the ECU, the affection that led Dr. Eric Williams to be named “the Doc” by some of his followers has mostly been supplanted by fear of varying degrees. Even before the loss of Grenada, Eric Williams' governance exhibited some authoritarian tendencies, but now he has embraced them.

Political parties, already hemmed in on all sides by the devotees of Eric Williams, are now violently suppressed, with the PRI model of pseudo-democracy supplanting the relatively functional system previously present. To that end, Williams' secret police, christened the “Flying Squads”, are being expanded to an unprecedented level and are now as ubiquitous as propaganda posters. Every act Williams takes these days evinces fear of an American-backed operation to overthrow him.
strings.TRI_Paging_Doc_Williams_desc:
Having been forced into making concessions by the United States in order to end the Greanada Crisis, the affection that led Dr. Eric Williams to be “the Doc” by some of his followers is increasingly supplanted by contempt; the very nickname itself is slowly turning into a pejorative.

His ambitions stymied, Williams has grown withdrawn and sullen, unwilling to partake in the work of government. Williams' pronunciations have lost all energy and sound more like boilerplate communiqués. Political opposition, formerly a pipe dream, now grows in the shadows as Williams no longer takes as much of a personal hand in governance. Meanwhile, the average citizen of the East Caribbean Union watches American companies get free reign and loses faith in the man once called “the Doc” as flattery; the personality cult has been blown away like all of Eric Williams' hopes and dreams.
strings.TRI_colonial_DEF: the Crown Colony of Trinidad and Tobago
strings.TRI_Founder_IT_desc:
GDP Growth Boost: 10%

Of all of the conquests and victories Italy enjoyed during the twentieth century, many consider the formation of the Triumvirate to be the greatest among them. The diplomatic pride and joy of the Empire, the Triumvirate is- on paper- merely a defensive pact around the Mediterranean for mutual protection against the German Reich to their north. In practice, however, it was a masterstroke for Italian foreign policy. Italy's central place in the Mediterranean, and the bounty from her overseas Empire has granted her the unofficial position of first among equals amidst the Triumvirate's Founders.

The alliance has been on the decline, and as Italy seems to be its primary beneficiary, she is also the nation that has been fighting the hardest to keep it intact. Their Iberian and Turkish allies have not seen the diplomatic fruits of the partnership though, and without drastic action, this Italian bloc in all but name may indeed be reduced to merely Italy and her puppets.
strings.TRI_Founder_IB_desc:
GDP Growth Boost: 10%

Of the three Founders of the Triumvirate, the Iberian Union faced the most direct peril at the hands of the rampaging Germans. They seized the former Portuguese colonies in Africa by force, after all, and then they tried to foist the Gibraltar dam upon them, a project that would have only brought misery upon Iberia and all the nations of the Mediterranean. What was a project in power projection for Italy and a way to shore up border concerns for Turkey was a matter of survival for Iberia, and as such Iberia fought for the formation and maintenance of the Triumvirate since its inception.

But times are different now. The Germans seem to be retracting inwards these days, or at least stagnating somewhat, and Iberia no longer feels the existential threat of the Reich loom over them so heavily anymore. Now it is the time to ask what Iberia's ambitions are, and whether or not the Triumvirate is conducive to those aims. And if it's not, then perhaps it might be time to graduate beyond being a supporting actor behind the Italians on the world stage.
strings.TRI_Founder_TR_desc:
GDP Growth Boost: 10%

The Republic of Turkey, unlike her western counterparts in Italy and Iberia, found herself aligning with the Italians and their Triumvirate not necessarily out of fear of the Germans to the north, but out of a need to secure their borders and foreign policy so they could focus on the nation's internal struggles. The Twentieth Century has seen great gains for the young republic, but with their massive successes, they have also gained much in the way of burdens, namely in the area of regional minorities that struggle ceaselessly against the nation. Turkey has needed breathing room to deal with these threats, and if nothing else the Triumvirate has provided exactly that.

But times change, and to survive, nations need to adapt to those changes. The Triumvirate is, to put it bluntly, a dying alliance. It no longer offers the security or support to Turkey that it once did, having evolved into a vanity project of Italian duces over the years. Turkey once again strains within her borders, and looks to break out of the constraints that the nature of their alliance places upon them.
strings.TRI_Member_desc:
GDP Growth Boost: 5%

There are three founders of the Triumvirate, that is where the name comes from after all. However, in spite of that, the alliance encompasses more than merely Italy, Iberia, Turkey, and their respective puppets. A number of smaller nations find themselves in the orbit of one or more of these secondary powers and have, for one reason or another, petitioned the Founders for induction into the Triumvirate as a junior partner.

These nations maintain their legal autonomy and independence, but find their interests largely subordinated to that of the “Big Three” members of the Triumvirate both economically and in terms of foreign policy. This is all, of course, in exchange for the protection and security that the Triumvirate provides. Even still, many consider the inclusion within the Triumvirate to be more of a burden than an aid, because while they maintain their technical sovereignty over their own borders, everyone knows that Rome, Istanbul, and Madrid hold significant sway over the politicians in every one of the minor nations that seek out the Triumvirate.
strings.TRI_Member_Client_desc:
GDP Growth Boost: -2.5%

Legally speaking, the various client states, puppet regimes, and regional authorities of the Triumvirate represent less of a junior or underclass of nations within the Triumvirate, and something more akin to tumors or growths off of their parent nations. The legal status of client states within the Triumvirate is murky, with the Founders desiring recognition for the full membership of their vassals, while also seeking to prevent the other two from doing the same.

For this reason, the status of clients and subordinate nations and regions will remain something of a grey area from now until the end of the alliance, which may be fast approaching. In spite of how little they truly gain from the alliance, the Triumvirate has thus far kept their master nations restrained and at peace with one another, but with the disintegration of the Triumvirate looking as likely as it is now, the smallest of nations have much to fear as the local juggernauts begin sharpening their knives...
strings.TRI_Observer_desc:
GDP Growth Boost: 2.5%

Where the Triumvirate's reach extends beyond the Mediterranean, there can be found the associated nations known as Triumvirate Observers. Though not formal members of the alliance, they still take part in its activities and benefit from mutual cooperation. Someday, these nations may seek to join the Triumvirate as full members... If the bloc can last that long, that is.
